subsystems.name: Quantum entropy source
subsystems.role: produces a physical process whose outcome is fundamentally unpredictable.

subsystems.name: Detection and timing
subsystems.role: measures the quantum event and converts it to an electronic signal.

subsystems.name: Raw bit generation
subsystems.role: turns each measurement into one or more bits.

subsystems.name: Randomness extraction
subsystems.role: removes bias and correlations so the output is close to perfectly uniform.
parts: Toeplitz matrix or other strong extractor

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: delivers the random bits as keys to encryption systems.

subsystems.name: Health and certification
subsystems.role: continuously tests the source and output so failures are detected.

buildSteps.title: Choose the quantum process
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether to measure photon arrival times, vacuum fluctuations or a split single photon; each gives different bit rates and robustness.

buildSteps.title: Build the optical path
buildSteps.detail: Align a laser, attenuate it to the single-photon level, and direct it to detectors on a temperature-stabilised bench.

buildSteps.title: Design the detection electronics
buildSteps.detail: Use SPADs or superconducting nanowire detectors with fast amplifiers and a time-to-digital converter to timestamp each event to picoseconds.

buildSteps.title: Generate raw bits
buildSteps.detail: Convert timestamps or detector outcomes into a raw binary stream; this stream is biased and must be processed.

buildSteps.title: Apply randomness extraction
buildSteps.detail: Run the raw bits through a strong extractor (e.g., a cryptographic hash or Toeplitz matrix) with a seed to produce near-uniform output.

buildSteps.title: Test and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Continuously run statistical tests on the output and monitor the source for tampering or drift.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with cryptography
buildSteps.detail: Feed the extracted bits into a hardware security module or software key store, where they become keys for encryption or authentication.

buildSteps.title: Package and certify
buildSteps.detail: Enclose the optics and electronics in a rugged, tamper-evident case for data-centre racks, or shrink to a chip for embedded use.

prerequisites.why: they register individual photons, which is essential for many quantum entropy sources.
well-studied algorithms remove bias from raw quantum measurements.
lasers, attenuators and beam splitters are off-the-shelf laboratory items.
HSMs and key stores can accept external entropy, but standardised interfaces are still maturing.
photonic integrated circuits have demonstrated QRNG, but widespread low-cost production is not yet routine.

pathway.milestone: rack-mounted quantum random number generators supply entropy to servers and HSMs
pathway.unlocks: high-quality keys for today's encryption, resistant to flaws in software pseudo-randomness.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale QRNG integrated into CPUs, smart cards and mobile systems-on-chip
pathway.unlocks: strong randomness everywhere, from phones to IoT devices.

pathway.milestone: combined QRNG and quantum key distribution (QKD) for long-distance links
pathway.unlocks: keys whose secrecy rests on quantum physics rather than computational hardness.

pathway.milestone: quantum entropy as a standard building block alongside post-quantum cryptography
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end security that resists both classical and quantum attacks, if QKD and PQC mature.
